The hostess, if you could even call her that, barely acknowledged my presence and pointed me toward a table that was already occupied. After a few awkward attempts to get her attention, I was finally seated—though not before I noticed a half-eaten plate of food on the table next to me.

My friend’s salad was riddled with wilted, discolored leaves and what looked like a piece of mold growing on the side of the bowl.

To make matters worse, when I brought the food back to the server, he looked at me like I had personally insulted his family and said, “That’s how it comes out.” I was told that the kitchen was “backlogged” and that we would have to wait another 45 minutes for a replacement. By that point, I was more than ready to leave.

I can't stress enough how disappointing this experience was. The food was not just bad—it was dangerous. The service was nonexistent, and the overall experience was one I will never forget, though I certainly hope to never repeat.

If you're looking for a place to eat, I strongly advise you to go somewhere else. *The Diner at Willow Street* is not a place for food, but rather a cautionary tale.
